name: Anapana — Counting Exhalations · Dawn Sit
description: Count each exhalation 1 to 10, then begin again. When lost, smile and restart at 1. Practice at first light when mind is fresh. Variation 1 of the Buddha's mindfulness-of-breathing, isolating counting exhalations so attention matures without overwhelm.
essence: Breathing in, I arrive. Breathing out, I release.
instructions: Sit erect yet soft; rock gently, then become still.
Establish attention: Count each exhalation 1 to 10, then begin again. When lost, smile and restart at 1.
Know each breath clearly without controlling it.
When distracted, label thinking and return kindly.
Widen to whole-body breathing near the end.
Dedicate merit: may all beings breathe freely.

Close with whole-body awareness and metta.

name: Walking — Lifting-Moving-Placing · Park Loop
description: Meditation in motion: lifting-moving-placing practiced on a park loop. The Buddha himself walked between sittings; movement wakes dullness and grounds restlessness.
essence: Peace is every step.
instructions: Stand; feel feet, balance, whole body.
Walk noting: lifting-moving-placing.
Feel heel, sole, toes; weight shifting.
At path end pause, turn mindfully.
Expand to whole body moving in space.
End standing in gratitude.

instructions: Begin mindful tea drinking with one conscious breath.
Do one thing at a time, fully.
Feel sensations: texture, temperature, sound.
When rushing, pause and smile.
End with gratitude for the activity.
Carry the calm to the next act.
source: Thich Nhat Hanh — Miracle of Mindfulness
